utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes, Mr. Karadzic you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Excellencies. Good morning to all. Thank you, thank you for giving me this opportunity. I come from a system where it was clear for 50 years that if somebody is sentenced to ten years in prison, he must be guilty of something because for nothing people got eight years in prison. That was our justice; however, the west hasn't faired much better. When it was established that Dreyfus, totally innocent, life imprisonment was reduced to ten years in prison. So we've got two systems that have similar results. They are particularly drastic and dangerous when they meet one another: Western justice and our Balkan fate. Something like that happened in the beginning of the 20th century when Austro-Hungary tried many Serbs. The best known were the Banja Luka and Zagreb trials that really shamed that country. And then Masaryk and other renowned persons with a great deal of moral integrity were turned against the state because the state acted in such a way. The Dreyfus affair and the Austro-Hungarian trials happened then. And, in the meantime, nothing that big or this wrong happened like this war that was imposed upon us and these trials that followed that war. From those days until today, until this case, there hasn't been a situation when so many decent, innocent people, mostly Serbs, were sentenced to high prison sentences that they are serving in different European countries outside their homeland; and, on the other side, so many perpetrators of crimes against Serbs, murderers, were set free. We can pretend that that did not happen, but it did happen, and it will be remembered for longer than the Dreyfus affair. And that will be studied; everything that was done and how justice was meted out. We know exactly why that was done in 1914, for the sake of the Austrian breakthrough into the east, why that is being done towards the end of the 20th century. With small nations, that we don't know. Let us hope to God that this is just for the sake of NATO credibility or different elections. But I'm afraid that that is on account of something that is far bigger than that and that the entire world is going to pay for a lot more. To be honest towards the Trial Chambers, although the Judgements and the elaborations provided by different Trial Chambers, are really something that should be read and that one had to wonder at, how people reach certain conclusions. I have to say that the Trial Chambers are less guilty there because that is really the handiwork of the Prosecutor's office. For example, in this case, the Prosecutor is challenging the authenticity of the Serb fear of a new genocide, and they say that that was imposed upon the people by Karadzic and the Serb Democratic Party. There is not a single family that does not have living witnesses or the offspring of those who were killed in the genocide that took place in the Second World War. It would only be fair for the Prosecution to come out and say that had there not been a genocide against Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia 50 years ago, now it's been longer than that but in relation to 1990 it would have been 50 years, then Karadzic and others would not have to defend themselves and they would not have to explain why they were not actually trying to convince the people of something that is wrong and that is not well-founded. The Prosecution did not err on the side of caution. They did even more than they were allowed to do. In our system, the Prosecution would not be allowed to do what was done in this Tribunal, in this case more particularly. I'm more familiar with my own case. They would have been cautioned. Perhaps the case would have been thrown out all together because of the way in which it is being presented to the Chamber. Now, what is all this about? I know the truth. The Prosecution knows the truth. Who are we supposed to delude? The Trial Chamber. If I were a member of the Trial Chamber, I would be offended. This degree of falsifying facts, such bastardised sentences where only portions of sentences given in response are being taken into account and then this semantic bastard is being presented as a fact. I highly appreciated the well-intentioned cautions issued by the Trial Chamber that I was not defending the Serb people but that I was here to defend myself because the Serb people were not on trial; however, you will see that it is the Serb people who stand accused, the entire Serb people stands accused, and that has been demonstrated over the past two days most tellingly. This is how it is being done: The Prosecution cannot indicate what my motives are for those actions that they are attributing to me, to my friends, my collaborators, and the entire Serb community in Bosnia and Herzegovina, this community consisting of 1.500.000 people. I did not have any reasons to go into politics actively. I had a successful professional career, a very nice one. Also as a physician, as a doctor, I had a loving family, I had a good social network, including many Muslims and Croats. Many of them remained my friends. As I'm a trained psychiatrist and I received my training in England, the US, in Yugoslavia, and Belgrade, Zagreb, Sarajevo, and also knowing the Russian and English languages, I could have worked anywhere in the world. I was not a candidate for any particular office. Now, why did I do all of this? If I'm crazy, then the Trial Chamber has to see whether I am responsible for my actions. If it is a question of patriotism being equated with craziness, then the Trial Chamber has to see what the Prosecution is doing. If I'm crazy, are a million and a half Serbs crazy, who let their only sons go into freezing trenches to defend their homes and families for three and a half years? To vote at all referenda in favour of what the Serb Democratic Party advocated and what I personally advocated? Did they have a motive? Did the Prosecution show to the Trial Chamber in any way what it was that happened? How come so many people agreed on this? Out of 12 million Serbs throughout the world, at least 8 million stood by that policy -- or rather, was opposed to the policy that was pushing us into war and into defending our basic fundamental rights. The Prosecution has really exaggerated here, the distinguished Mr. Tieger. He said that I said that the SDS was full of idiots. The SDS had within itself and behind it the elite of the Serb people, university professors, academicians, writers, doctors, and there would be some obstinate people too, and colloquially we could say that such a person was an idiot but not really. This kind of membership made the SDS the best party, the most self-sacrificing party among the Serb people and throughout Europe, if you will. The dissidents who had the moral strength to oppose Tito and communism now made an effort in favour of their own people, and they opposed the new world order that did not take into account the basic interests of the Serbs. The luckier ones lost their property but the less-fortunate ones lost their nearest and dearest. The Prosecution offends these people deeply by the things they are saying, by fabricating this joint criminal enterprise that involves these people too, because these people asked to be represented honestly and to have their political objectives and their struggle for freedom be represented and defended. Nobody could have imposed that upon the Serbs. The Serbs are the most difficult people to lead because they are not sheep. They are not obedient. So nothing can be imposed on them just like that. These weak allusions proffered by the Prosecution are trying to lead the Trial Chamber astray. Various words that were uttered by MPs over the phone and chitchat, et cetera, and then they're drawing conclusions on the basis of that. And then the entire case and the entire Judgement, therefore, is supposed to be based on conclusions, based on hearsay evidence. That would really be another invention, another precedent which would, indeed, be remembered. Allusions, inferences, instead of evidence, that judgements would be made on that basis. For example, as a matter of fact, certain sentences uttered by members of parliament are being misquoted here, although we heard two prime ministers here, Lukic and Djeric. There were some extreme opinions presented in debates, sometimes motived by political reasons, but these extremist views never prevailed. The parliament does not meet for the sake of sentences. The parliament meets to produce documents that would be the foundation of a system. They did not show us a single document of the Assembly of Republika Srpska that would have tolerated crime, let alone led to crime as such. The distinguished Mr. Tieger, a distinguished lawyer from the Prosecution, since he has no evidence he decided to tarnish my personality and he called me a liar and a mobster. That happened on the very first day, and this was front page news in our media, as the strongest argument provided by the Prosecution. That frees me from any obligation to remain polite, but I'm not going to resort to that because I have arguments. I believe that it was with a heavy heart that Mr. Tieger decided to go for this kind of labelling and tarnishing a person's reputation. He probably wouldn't have done that had he had a single shred of hard evidence against Radovan Karadzic. In this way, without any kind of evidence, the OTP is expecting the Trial Chamber to make certain decisions, to draw certain conclusions, and to base the Judgement on that which the Prosecution is proffering as evidence, and this basically consists of allusions, random chitchat, testimony by their own employees as experts, who managed to put the indictment itself into evidence. We've written all of this. I don't need to repeat everything that we've said in the final brief, how the employees of the OTP testified, admitting that they made an effort to please the Prosecution, to prove something that the OTP already knows, and so on. We have about a dozen of those experts who, at any rate, should have been totally impartial and they certainly were not. Now, what is behind the Prosecution case, the so-called joint criminal enterprise? This was probably taken from legal provisions that deal with the prosecution of Mafia. There wouldn't have been an indictment had it not been for this kind of unfair argumentation. There would have been no indictments except for immediate perpetrators. If you don't believe this, instruct the Prosecution to write up a -- or to patch up an indictment against me that would exclude JCE. Let's see what Karadzic would stand accused of then, apart from the joint criminal enterprise. The only thing that would remain would be my good deeds, towards my own people and towards the other two peoples. These good deeds are reflected in major efforts to avoid a war, and also in lessening the suffering of all three peoples once the war had broken out. Honest persons, especially those who converse with God, know that that is so, honest persons from all three ethnic communities. The Prosecution adheres to the JCE, thus accusing each and every Serb. It is not true that the entire Serb people is not being accused because this trial - and not only this one, these trials in general - are supposed to shift responsibility from other peoples to the Serb people, and then after the Jewish people some other people are supposed to be declared victims to simply change this overall perception of crimes in the world, as it stands today. The Prosecution did not come up even with approximate allusions as to who and how founded this joint criminal enterprise, who determined what would happen and what would be done by whom. The OTP draws conclusions after a civil war happened, after crimes were committed in that civil war, so they say that must be because the Serbs had founded the Serb Democratic Party in 1990. Then, however, they abandoned this idea that it was the beginning of the JCE, and they move it to 1991 and the moment when the authorities were established after these elections. And then they blacken our entire struggle for freedom, constitutionality, and the rule of law, as if on all other sides the rule of law and honesty and integrity towards partners were flourishing, as if there had been no secret army founded on the other side, targeting exclusively Bosnian Serbs, an army that was first intended to fight the JNA and Yugoslavia and then Bosnian Serbs. We've heard here many accusations against completely legal actions in parliamentary life and lawful parliamentary decisions. I am painted by the Prosecution as an autocrat who holds everything in his own hands, although there is hard evidence that it's not me calling people from the Ministry of the Interior; they were calling me to ask me about the agreement I had made with the SDA and the HDZ, and they were afraid of it because that agreement threatened the foundations of our state and the provisions of that agreement were incompatible with the survival of the Serbian people. And I hope the record will be corrected after we hear the tapes. So the Prosecution implies that the Serb Democratic Party should not have cared about implementing the programme that was supported by 50 per cent of the vote, although the Serbian Democratic Party put in positions of power the least amount of party cadres, and that's why I was criticised by many Prosecution witnesses, including Neskovic and others, who claimed that I had put power back into the hands of old cadres, although I had tried to nominate professional and able people. Thus, everything that happened in 1990 turns out to be suspect, whereas the Islamic Declaration is mentioned nowhere. I had asked Mr. Izetbegovic explicitly, and he said that he would not renounce it for the sake of our political life in Bosnia-Herzegovina. They pretend there had been no decision to establish the Patriotic League on the 30th of March, 1991, and as if on the 30th of April, 1991, that league had not really been established, and that's the date from which their years of service are counted, as if the council for the defence of Muslims had not been established, comprising officials who, instead of defending Bosnia and all the ethnic communities, created a separate body as a political wing of the Patriotic League. They pretend that until September -- by September 1991, as if we -- as we saw from the documents of Sefer Halilovic, the Patriotic League was not established in 103 joint municipalities. They only didn't dare to establish them in Croat communities. And in those communities, in many of them, Serbs were the majority; 8 per cent were the Muslim majority. And if all that had not been happening, the Serbs were trying to do something that was prohibited. And the Prosecution completely overlooks the willingness of the Serbs to compromise, and they ignore our demands to form associations of municipalities by their own free will. Instead, we see that there are orders to form joint municipalities in Kosovo. It was always the right of people to organise themselves and form associations, to combine their resources to meet their needs. Regionalisation is a red rag to the Prosecution, as if it had been done in secret. The regionalisation was carried out pursuant to the constitution and the laws, and especially in view of the threats that Bosnia would secede violently and unilaterally from Yugoslavia without dealing with the issues of the rights of Serbs, and later Croats as it turned out. The Prosecution overlooks that we accepted to give up on the regionalisation at the proposal of Mr. Zulfikarpasic. The international and our Western allies who regularly betray the Serbs - and they have done so this time - had the opportunity to opt for European-oriented Muslims in Bosnia. There are many of them, and there were two big parties led by Fikret Abdic and Zulfikarpasic. No, they opted for the other variant that led to war. The Prosecution says in their paragraph -- they say that Bosnia-Herzegovina inevitably moved towards independence while Karadzic was -- it's paragraph 28, Karadzic was intensifying ... and so on and so forth. Bosnia was not moving towards independence inevitably. It was not inevitable. But in chair's opinion number 4 says that. It was not inevitable and it was not clear. And we see that from the decision to establish a conference on Bosnia-Herzegovina lead by Lord Carrington and Ambassador Cutileiro. If it had been inevitable, why then all these additional measures to enable it? And although the Serbs had accepted to remain in an independent Bosnia, on the condition that they continue to enjoy at least a part of what had been provided by the former joint state of Yugoslavia, that proposal was supported by the European community. That was a condition sine qua non. Without that, Bosnia could not have moved towards independence. That was accepted, and within a week an attempt was made to trick us. We saw what Irfan Ajanovic was saying on the 18th of March. "We will yet see who is a fool, who is fooling the European community, who is not in favour in peace." Since that did not happen within a week, it was the SDA that rejected the agreement, Irfan Ajanovic later said that they only needed to gain time, and why did they need that time? To trick the Serbs. The Prosecution says that the Serbs had grabbed 65 or 70 per cent of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Serbs demanded that much for themselves, and they rely on different scribes serving at various conferences and their understanding. But it is not confirmed by Cutileiro or Akashi or anybody else who testified, it's nowhere in the papers. On the contrary, Lord Owen says that it would have been the first instance in history that an army that has not been defeated would give back so much of the territory that it was at that moment controlling and holding. Let's look into these territorial issues. The Prosecution claims that we were taking over power in different places and that we had conquered 65 or 70 per cent of the territory. The evidence is replete with proof that we had had that territory even before the war, and we had an even larger territory before the war. And I said many times in the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina: Don't try to violently impose some sort of new state. That state will not be able to impose its power on 65 per cent on Bosnian territory. Nobody ever disputed that Serbs were the majority in 65 per cent of Bosnian territory and that the Serb ownership in Bosnia-Herzegovina was about 64 per cent. We heard here that the late President Milosevic was smirking at the idea, saying it was social property. If the Prosecution had looked into our legislation, they would have seen that it was not state property. It was social property, and farmland belonged to peasants. Other people could not use it as grazing land unless they had an agreement with the peasants. It's not nobody's; it's somebody's property. However, in 1990, at the elections, the Serbs won absolute power in 37 per cent of municipalities, rural but rather well-developed municipalities, and a good amount of the vote in 47 per cent of the municipalities. The Prosecution says that the joint criminal enterprise implied take-over of power in municipalities in which we already had power; and in the municipalities in which we had power and in municipalities where we were a minority party, there were conditions to form two or three different municipalities. Even when we created the provisional borders of Republika Srpska, we invited Croats and Muslims to establish their own police stations wherever possible, not to go into Serb villages, and the Serbs would not go into their villages to defuse tensions. There is no way to throw out somebody from a municipality in which they have their own police station, their own municipal authority. That was not the purpose. The purpose was for the Serbs to protect what they already had, and the Prosecution says here that Karadzic had said he would not allow Alija's state to operate. Of course that kind of state would not work because the Serbs would not accept it. But a state in which one-third of the population occupying two-thirds of the territory as a majority populace can function and will function, and I must mention that it was late Mr. Izetbegovic who first suggested to divide Bosnia and who proposed to apply his Islamic ideas only on the Muslim part of the territory. He was then pushed into war. Somebody pushed him into war. The conspiracy core inside the SDA pushed him. Zulfikarpasic discovered it, as did some European countries. We will find out about that. Zulfikarpasic left the SDA at that moment. It was anyway Mr. Izetbegovic who suggested to divide Bosnia, and I informed President Milosevic about that in an intercept reported on 29 May 1991. It's D -- we have it on the screen now. We were astounded and we were not prepared because we had not been thinking about this at all. However, when it became clear that they will not abandon the idea of Bosnia's independence and they mean to have a unitary Bosnia ruled by a regime that was unacceptable to us, then we accepted it on the condition that we also have independence. The Prosecution says that Karadzic was spreading the perception of threats against Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but the Prosecution does not want to show to the Trial Chamber that in the Muslim part and the Croat-held part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it was Hitler's Allies who came into power. If not President Tudjman, then his collaborators who came back from emigration and took power. And Mr. Izetbegovic, beginning with 1939, were members of the young Muslim movement and received al-Husseini, the mufti who arrived to prepare the Handschar Division as Hitler's ally and personal friend. Those were the things that all the intelligentsia among the Serbs, all the educated people knew and wanted to defend the Serb people from that, rather than conquer other peoples villages or territory or impose their will on somebody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, now because of -- thanks to that video aid, we know that it's part of Exhibit D1282, but for the future reference, you're better to put it on the record, in the future. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I apologise. For the transcript, it's D1282 of the 29th of May, 1991. So the OTP, without the obligation, to actually determine who concocted this joint criminal enterprise wants the Trial Chamber to believe it. They say Karadzic wanted an ethnically pure Republika Srpska on 60 to 70 per cent of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, although the record is replete with evidence that what that was about was the creation of homogenous territory by not taking the inhabited places of others and the regions belonging to others as part of the Republika Srpska. All that time, Karadzic in the parliament of the Bosnian Serbs, in the parliament of Republika Srpska, was fighting against coveting territories, exaggerated territorial claims, and I quoted Mr. Izetbegovic, who said "by God" -- this is P12. I believe that it is page 38, where Mr. Izetbegovic said: "For God's sake. When drawing the maps, please try to have the least possible number of us in your parts and the least possible number of your people in our parts." This is a way to homogenise territories at the time when nobody was even considering the possibility of war breaking out because there was agreement that the problem should be addressed by not being overly predatory and greedy in respect of territories belonging to others. So what happened was that before the war, Dobratici, a group of Croatian villages from the Skender Vakuf municipality, later Knezevo, in the presence of European monitors was actually separated from Knezevo with its Serbian majority on a voluntarily basis, and it was annexed to Jajce with a Croatian majority. However, the Prosecution is accusing Mr. Koljevic, an exceptional person, dubbing him a Serb nationalist, extremist, and in paragraph 75 accuses him that he had said that the Serbs had accepted changes of internal borders in order to accommodate ethnic reality. Changes of internal borders meant what Mr. Izetbegovic was talking about, what I was talking about, and on which such agreement had been reached even before the war, and such a transaction had already been conducted between two municipalities. So one group could not be retained by force of Croatian villages in a majority Serbian municipalities if they felt better and could meet their interests better in another municipality, and that was done. The Prosecution goes on to abuse and to falsify data that it has. How does it do that when in the Assembly of Republika Srpska I advocated the acceptance of a plan, and when I spoke that or said that we should not fight for too much territory, strive for too much territory, what happened was that I am -- it is -- I'm depicted as having said I did not want Muslims and Croats in the state. That never referred to Muslims and Croats who would remain with us. That always meant -- that was always directed against any requests for every Croatian village to be made part of Republika Srpska because that would have meant misunderstandings, it would have meant that people who would have become part of such a state would have become enemies of that state, would not feel comfortable in it, and we would not have their agreement generally speaking. Where Yugoslavia is concerned, that's our common house, our bitter agreement to Croatia's seceding from Yugoslavia by saying that we should not fight at any cost for our enemies to remain in our house who have attacked us in that century twice. The OTP portrays this as if we were talking about domestic Muslims in Bijeljina, Srbac, Janja, or any other place where they could, if they so wanted to, live normal lives. This is what I talk about in Exhibit P87. I'll read it in English. [In English] "When we sacrifice the state for the sake of one village that wants to join it, if we start blowing like the balloon, we can easily burst and we don't have the right to do that." [Interpretation] I was saying exactly the same things in respect of the mistake committed in 1980 by late King Aleksandar, when he accepted that future big Yugoslavia, the Kingdom of the Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes, when he agreed to accept Croats and Slovenes into that state and create at an inopportune moment a multinational state when you could not create a state out of a tribe. That was not a job to be done in the 19th century. That didn't happen in the 20th century. I apologise. Actually, it was page 87 and the exhibit is D92 when I talked about the sacrifices made for a village. So this position against coveting the territories of others, against such greed for territory and exaggerated greed, is -- so my position against it is mischaracterised. That, actually, I was saying that what -- we should expel the Croats and Muslims from what we were holding. The record is full of evidence that the Serbian side had accepted and, in fact, had itself proposed and accepted to protect the minorities in the cantons and in the republics, which the European community had brokered upon a reciprocal basis and in a decent and humane way. There is not a single shred of evidence that the Serbs wanted anything but that. The Trial Chamber in the Krajisnik case actually highlighted a paragraph, I believe it was paragraph 109, where in respect of my words which I uttered on the 14th of February, 1992, after the 13th of February when we had established that there would be three Bosnias with Cutileiro, so my words that they should be aware that there should be no escaping from our parts, that Trial Chamber determined that, at that time, Karadzic was still taking care of other -- of the interests of the others, of the Muslims and the Croats. If we looked at the decision of that Trial Chamber of this Tribunal, prior to that there was no joint criminal enterprise. We actually have to set a new birthday for the joint criminal enterprise, but they cannot show it to exist. They can say there were murders that must have been according to plan, and they take this KDZ240, (redacted) who, was not supposed to testify about things that he knew nothing about, they take him as a witness who says: I first thought that Karadzic had a great analytical ability and then I actually realised that he was telling me that what he was planning would actually happen. And I say that that is not so. And I refer to my address to the Assembly -- speech to the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 15th of October, 1991, which the OTP yesterday again represented this as a threat, although it is an imminently anti-war address. I actually anticipated what would happen if we opt for forcible secession, the forcible secession of unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina from Yugoslavia. I reiterated that on -- also on the 25th of January, 1992, when I had this brief exchange with Muhamed Cengic. We actually agreed to postpone the referendum until such time as the government will have carried out the regionalisation. I told him: We all know what will happen if an inter-ethnic -- a civil war breaks out here, there will be massive loss of life. The Serbs will flee to their parts, the Croats to their parts, and the Muslims to their parts. And what will we get? What will we gain? The same thing that we have now, but it will be much more homogenised, and we will have to sit down and sign an agreement. In the meantime, there will be several hundred thousand dead, several hundred cities demolished, and we shall be where we stand today. We shall have to sit down and ensure three signatures. Without three signatures, there is no Bosnia. That was not clairvoyance. That was just simple watching what was happening in -- following what was happening in Croatia, what was happening, what had happened in all our lands in every war. Witnesses of the Prosecution -- for the Prosecution here have confirmed that every war in the lands of the former Yugoslavia had a civil component, a civil war component, where our people, brethren of the same blood, same kinship, but of different religions, exterminated each other.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: So such my actions involving exchanges with foreigners are portrayed as this or that, as if Karadzic had confessed. I cannot confess, I cannot deny it, because I don't know until an investigation has been carried out, or at least an inquiry to the military whether it had, indeed, been so. So because of -- in the absence of real guilt and real evidence, the OTP is actually portraying this as my confession. Colm Doyle testified that I said that -- that they should not open fire on Television Sarajevo, and I told him they will not shoot. Somebody shooting, I don't know whether these are Serb forces, and he said Karadzic accepted and apologised. But Karadzic, at that moment, was not in command of anything. He didn't have any army to -- under him. There were Territorial Defence forces of each municipalities. There were individuals. There was the JNA - and I was not in command of the JNA - and the OTP says Karadzic ensured that they shoot on Television Sarajevo, that fire be opened on Television Sarajevo in April 1992. So these are manoeuvres, and there is not a single allegation of the OTP which does not need to be verified for veracity, for truthfulness of the allegation. Yesterday reference was made how I was accusing Beara and Mladic because I was not guilty of something, but this is unheard of. This is something I never did. I never defended myself by accusing others, and I never accused anybody else of Srebrenica because I don't know what happened. Now the picture is being put together, but that is not my defence. In my opening remarks, I said I will not defend myself but by pointing the finger of blame at other people. What I want is, I want to know what happened, and I know what happened. Civil war happened that we could have anticipated, that we saw before that in Croatia. So it is a sea, an ocean, it is an abundance of things. There is not a single sentence that should not be exposed to criticism because this is not the way this is done -- actually, misleading the Trial Chamber. This is not in the service of justice, distorting words and sentences, is not that. Yesterday they said that it is not true that there was no communication between Pale and Sarajevo and Banja Luka and that I didn't have influence, and they showed this telephone conversation between me and Brdjanin from November 1991. Nobody is saying that at that time there were no communications. KDZ101 - Dragan Kezunovic, not a protected witness - he said that instead of several thousand telegrams a day, there were about ten telegrams a day at the beginning of the war. That, that is called the communications were down [as interpreted]. So the Trial Chamber and the Defence tried, albeit it is in an unfavourable position, the Trial Chamber should actually check everything that the Prosecution is saying and proffering. They said yesterday Karadzic said that the incident in Kravica was triggered by an ostensible mutiny and then a thousand men were executed, shot to death in Kravica, as if Karadzic had said and then had them executed. First of all, it is not a thousand; and, secondly, it was established here that there had been an incident. So these are things - I'm looking at the clock - but these are things that are completely on a collision course with any notion of justice, not to say international justice. In our country, in the former system, this would not have been permitted to them. Just a sweeping statement, there was this JCE between me and President Milosevic. What we had was respect, at least on my part, but there was no agreement in any other thing, on any other -- in any other respect. He was against the creation of Republika Srpska; we were in favour of the creation of Republika Srpska. He was against the establishment of the Assembly of the Serbian people; I was in favour of that assembly. And we have evidence here to that effect, because we didn't any longer have a chamber of nations. He was in favour of accepting all or any peace plans. I have never seen many of the alleged members of the JCE in my life, but the Prosecution believes that they have no obligation to identify and state how and in what manner was this plan which is being attributed to us actually drawn up and developed. So I am looking at the clock, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break. Before that, yes, Judge Morrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, you've been competing with what sounds like a powerful electric drill. We will see if we can get it silenced, but I can't guarantee that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Registry will take a look into that. We will have a break for 20 minutes and resume at 22 past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As for the transcript and for the Trial Chamber too, could my indication of the mistakes made by the Prosecution in terms of proving joint criminal enterprise, could that be translated and could that be in the transcript, primarily when was the joint criminal enterprise established or formed and then how and so on and so forth? They're going to trip over the fact - "they," the Prosecution - are going to trip over the fact that the Serbs kept giving concessions all the time in order to prevent a war. We have superb evidence here. The late Vance - not Harland who takes notes. In 1992 he informed Genscher that Dr. Karadzic wishes to avoid war at all costs. How would it be possible to realise any kind of joint criminal enterprise without a war? A JCE as represented by the OTP. However, the Prosecution says, and keeps saying, that the Serbs were not supposed to have any claims of their own as far as Bosnia is concerned, that they were overdoing it, and so on and so forth. The Prosecution is referring to some purported interview given by the late Raskovic, a friend of mine, a colleague of mine. They say that he gave an interview to Yutel, this TV station that was not exactly objective or fair towards the Serbs. They say that he was different from me, that he thought that Bosnia would not be Serb aside, that the Serbs would not suffer genocide in Bosnia. That is in paragraph 118 and it is P6617 on page 2. The late Raskovic allegedly said: [In English] "It would not be genocide. Maybe it would not be Serbophile," talking about Bosnia, "and it would be Serbophobe, but it wouldn't be Serbocide either." [Interpretation] Why would the Serbs accept that their country, Bosnia-Herzegovina, should be Serbophobe? And who can guarantee that a Serbophobe Bosnia would not become Serbocide at a given point in time? Now let us see what -- not what Vox says, because Vox said in 1990 what would happen to Serbs in Islamic Bosnia, and a year later when they were criticised, they again published this text and said: Well, we were just joking a year ago. Such jokes are never told in Bosnia, also the way people do not talk about a rope in the home of a hanged person. We understood that and we were right. Take a look at this, take a look at what Ganic is saying to President Tudjman, D1143. That's the number. Ganic says: You know that the world is going to let us marginalise the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the same exhibit at another section he says: We are going to marginalise the Serb entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is that Serbophobe component, I guess. So it's not Vox, it's the number two man of the Muslim authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina who is saying that. He is saying he is going to marginalise the Serbs and that he's going to marginalise the Serb entity; whereas he and his people are planning to import 4 million Turks, the alleged descendents of Bosniaks, and regularly they are bringing in illegally Muslims from Sandzak just to vote there and their only objective is to artificially change the ethnic picture of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Prosecution says that it was Karadzic who wanted to change the ethnic picture of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And of course they are fabricating evidence, inventing it, because there is no proof of any such thing. The Prosecution regularly misquotes words that I uttered somewhere at some point in time. These are mainly political speeches, so this is a clash of opinions, of different views, also struggling in parliament against undemocratic views, and the experts Donia and Treanor themselves admit that I was facing major difficulties in parliament; however, every decision in parliament was unanimously adopted. It was adopted because it was changed during the debate. The Trial Chamber has our position in evidence. Democrats find solutions; whereas communists make decisions. That means that the proposal has to be changed until everyone finds it acceptable. That's the essence of democracy; whereas Donia and Treanor, the Prosecution experts, say that they did not see a single proposal of the Bosnian Serbs not get through parliament. Well, it's because it did not remain unchanged, because it was not imposed on the MPs, not that anything could have been imposed on them. The Prosecution says that I -- I -- well, that's paragraph 43 of their final trial brief. They say that this is a well-known thing: [In English] "-- stressed to his followers that Muslims could not live with others and that population transfer was the solution. The conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina..." This is quotation: "... conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina is basically a conflict among peoples, just as it was in the case between India and Pakistan and that's nothing new. It resulted in a huge resettlement of the people." [Interpretation] That's the paragraph. That's what it sounds like. P938. This is what it says. It is page 36, like P12, page 18 through 20: [In English] "Imagine the stupidity ..." [Interpretation] I said how idiotic, imagine how idiotic this is, that's what I said in the original, how idiotic it would be to create war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. [In English] "The conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina is basically a conflict among peoples, just as it was the case between India and Pakistan and that's nothing new." [Interpretation] And then this is what it says: [In English] "Settlement." [Interpretation] I didn't say it resulted. [In English] "And with a huge resettlement or exchange of people." [Interpretation] So that's my position towards the instigation of inter-ethnic wars and population resettlements. However, this was butchered by the Prosecution and they are misrepresenting it, saying that on the 14th of February, 1992 -- actually, this was earlier -- or, no, later. But the 14th of February as well, 1992, that is P12, that I said that Muslims could not live with others. However, they omit to say that where fundamentalism arrives people cannot live together and that was the key point, the key sentence. The Prosecution says that earlier on I said that we live together, and so on and so forth. Yes, we lived together. However, I encouraged people to live together and now this thing that I said about fundamentalism. In the meantime, fundamentalism happened. They took power. The SDA gave up on Yugoslavia. They opted for unilateral secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina, even at the expense of peace. They sacrificed peace. The SDA formed a secret army consisting of over 100.000 people in 93 mixed municipalities. We saw all of that. The SDA secretly sent its members to Croatia for training, just as the Ustashas did before the Second World War, to Janka Puszta and Hungary where they trained people to slaughter Serbs. Then after one year of a terrible experience, deceit, abuse, abuse of institutions, abuse of police powers, then the Serbs realised that when this form of political Islam arrives, that form of government co-existence becomes impossible, living together becomes impossible. We can only live one next to the other. We were in favour of living one next to the other but not within the same political system. If the Chamber were to follow what was happening -- what is happening right now in Bosnia-Herzegovina, it is only Serbs that are being tried and there are video-clips of the crimes committed by Muslim generals and they're not even being indicted. They're putting that off. It's the same political system and there is that intention of abuse, of subjugating others. That is not recommendable and that is not conducive to a life together. However, the Prosecution portrays the Serbs as vagabonds, who are sticking a thorn into a healthy leg in peacetime. What I quoted is a verse by Njegos, and Njegos was indeed abused here, and that is a fact that the Prosecution did not make an effort to get semantic interpretations of our sayings, allusions, irony. When somebody says that we were the most active in having the Muslims move out and if you do not see that they are actually criticising the government, that they're not doing anything else, this is what they say about Zvornik, Bijeljina, this is irony, this is sarcasm, and the OTP are presenting this as bragging, as boasting. When I quote Njegos's verses, if you were to put them all in one pot, a broth could not be blended together. This is poetry from "The Mountain Wreath" that has been admitted into evidence. I cannot find the page reference right now, but this is a verse by Njegos, just like what I referred to earlier on was. But in somebody else's language, a person cannot understand that but they should have made an effort to get this interpreted properly rather than dragging Njegos through court. In paragraph 44, the Prosecution says when referring to talks within the Presidency of Yugoslavia in January 1993 and after the testimony of Minister Jovanovic here, the Prosecution still abides by their own total misinterpretations of what they -- of what was said there: [In English] "To remove non-Serbs from Serb-claimed areas and maintain a revised ethnic structure persisted after much of the forced displacement and that had taken place." [Interpretation] First of all, the structure was not changed because the obligation to return was always proposed by the Serb side and guaranteed as well. The Prosecution takes as a basis for JCE, for which they cannot say who established it and when. They say actually that the essence of this is the Serb intention of removing Croats and Muslims from territories that the Serbs aspire after, because during the war removing civilians from areas of combat is an obligation, then the Prosecution thought of saying permanent removal and then they added forcible removal in order to ensure that this indeed constitutes a crime. The removal of Muslims and Croats from territories that the Serbs aspire after - which is not a crime - was never the plan of the Serbs; rather, it was the struggle of Karadzic, Krajisnik, and all others not to grab too much, that we should not take five Muslim villages for the sake of one Serb village and that we should not create disgruntled people, that is paragraph 46 where the Prosecution says in their brief that I said that the Drina is pure. This is a discussion where we are preparing for a conference and we are wondering what the conference is going to give us, what they're going to agree to. It doesn't mean clean as in ethnically cleansed, it means clear, that it will not be in dispute. It's not that the Muslims didn't want the Drina. The Muslims wanted the fall of Srebrenica, they wanted to exchange it for Vogosca and Ilijas beforehand. Mr. Izetbegovic offered that to the people from Srebrenica; however, they refused. So when we say purely Serb territories, it doesn't mean cleansed Serb territories, it means indubitably Serb territories. Cleansed is not the same as clean or pure. There is a significant difference there. So you can see from the context that I am speaking about what awaits us at the conference in Dayton, what will be accepted, and for what we will have to struggle. In defence of the Owen-Stoltenberg plan in 1993, I was defending that plan before the MPs because they were saying some Serb towns and municipalities, 90 or 100 per cent Serbs, are not anymore in the Serb territory in the valley of the Neretva River, et cetera, and I told them: Look, let's be honest, we also got some places where we were not a majority. And the Prosecution portrays this as my bragging about the success in grabbing other people's territories; whereas I was persuading the parliament to accept the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan. It was partly unfair to us too, but it can't be fair only to us. In the same municipalities along the Drina River before the war and when the war began, we were offering to the Muslims to establish their own municipalities. Bratunac and Vlasenica had signed an agreement and made a map -- in fact, maps. And then somebody from Sarajevo ordered that they be rejected. So no word about driving people out or taking over power. We already had power. In Zvornik a plan had been made for two municipalities to exist, and to this day two municipalities exist as they did during the war. A large part of the Zvornik municipality was always controlled by the Muslims and we never tried to take that. However, the OTP claims that the Serbs took over Zvornik municipalities and that's not true. When the war began, then the Serbs took over the town itself along with the Serb parts, which in peacetime could have had two administrative municipalities in its urban core. In reference to Bratunac, it is said that somebody claimed there was no longer a single Muslim left in Bratunac. At that point the Serbs were controlling only the town and 20 per cent of the municipalities. 80 were in Muslim hands all the way up to October 1993. In that way, you can condemn anybody if you do not have the obligation to prove facts. We had to travel to Bratunac through Serbia because there was no direct communication. Everything was occupied. And Podrinje was in the Muslim hands for one whole year, occupied by at least 30.000 soldiers. These are their facts. They are in the case file, in evidence. And it was constantly a combat zone. The Serbs were suffering attacks in Podrinje for a whole year and for a whole year we appealed to them not to go on with it and that this area would eventually end up in the Muslim entity. In all plans, I always allowed the possibility and it was always drawn into every plan, the Vance Plan and the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan, it was always envisaged that Muslims would have 80 per cent of the territory in the Drina Valley. That was envisaged and it would have been so had they not opted for war. We will discuss Srebrenica tomorrow. Your Excellencies, I have to point out the chronology of events. The Muslims set fire to the valley of the Drina River at the very beginning of the month of April. The crisis was created there on the 31st of March. We saw a document here of the Croatian intelligence service and the Croatian Defence Council, showing that Captain Taric was sent to Bijeljina on the 31st of March to take over power. And then he really captured Bijeljina, took control of it. His snipers controlled the entire town from the water-tower and from the high-rises. The first victims fell, including a woman on her balcony, and then the Crisis Staff of that municipality, not the SDS Crisis Staff, got together to discuss what to do next. And then the OTP claims that the SDS invited Arkan to come to Bijeljina. I believe even the -- in the indictment and the pre-trial brief they say the crisis started when Arkan crossed the border. Arkan crossed the border 15 hours after combat started, and on that very day Arkan himself told the reporter: "We came at the invitation of the Territorial Defence of Semberija and the people." A year later in another interview, he said: We were invited by the SDS, because the SDS at that time was equated with the Serbian people. I have to find that sentence. But on that day Arkan said what he said, that he had been invited by the Territorial Defence, the Territorial Defence of Semberija. And of course, they not only failed to mention this, they falsified. And Prosecution chooses what he said two years later to present as the truth, not what he said on that very day. At the same time - and this is happening on the 31st of March - Karadzic has no power at all. There is still a joint Presidency in place. Biljana Plavsic and Fikret Abdic go at that time to Bijeljina to take care of the situation on behalf of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not on behalf of the SDS. And all this was going on a few days after the massacre against Serbs in Sijekovac, in Bosanski Brod. And what does it have to do with Radovan Karadzic or the SDS? And it is overlooked that the party Crisis Staff is something quite different to the Crisis Staff of the municipality. And five years into this trial they keep insisting that the Crisis Staff of the party grew later into the Crisis Staff of the municipality as a state agency. Yes, the same people were gathered in it, but it's not the same thing. And in Bijeljina there is absolutely no doubt who started it, who started the fighting and the crisis and with what intentions. Also overlooked is the fact that among the 42 or so casualties, less than 10 Serbs were included, but that's only because the Serbs had escaped and the Muslims had check-points around the town. They were exposed to bullets, to fire, the fire that was opened in response to their fire. I ask for your indulgence until I find the number of the document. And they keep insisting that the SDS took over power in Bijeljina on some day in April, the 2nd or the 3rd of April, after this conflict began. Although witnesses from Bijeljina confirmed here that there was no change in government, nobody took over power. The same authorities were in place on the 31st of January, 1991, as on the 31st of January, 1995. There was no take-over. It is also said here that Karadzic awarded Arkan, gave him a medal. Arkan never decorated -- Arkan was never decorated by Karadzic. He was decorated according to a proposal to decorate a unit consisting of two detachments, and that was a unit that was not in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1995 or in 1992, and in 1995 when they offered their services they were accepted and they were placed under the command of the army and the police and there was no love lost between that unit, Arkan's unit, and the army. The Prosecution claims that Karadzic had the judiciary, the investigating authorities, police, et cetera, he could have made arrests and punished people. The president did not have such powers. Kovac was asked here: If you had the authorities, the agencies, why didn't you tell the president so that he can do that? And he said: No, that's not the president's job. He didn't have such powers. He organises work in state authorities. He cannot interfere with the work of the ministries if the ministries are not going their job -- if they are doing their job; if they are not, then he can try to reorganise them. However, the Prosecution did not even care to look into the constitution and the legislation that governs the conduct of the president of the republic, but they do accept at the remark of one prime minister, saying that the ministers of the army, police, and justice did address the president. When there is a war on of course it is the obligation of these ministers to address the president to see how these organs are going to be resubordinated to the army because that needs presidential approval. The Prosecution claims there is evidence that Arkan had committed crimes but they didn't show that evidence. They wanted the president to make arrests and judge people based on their reputation. We had a lady witness here from Grbavica who had seen Vojvoda Aleksic accompanying Dr. Seselj and she jumped up and said: Here is Vojvoda Aleksic. I asked her: Do you know of any crime committed by Aleksic? She said: No. Aleksic has a reputation because he is called Vojvoda and he has a long beard, but he is an honest man, modest and humble man. Or concerning this Vlaske from Ilijas who was unpleasant to UNPROFOR and the monitors. He didn't care for them, didn't like them. He thought they were partial. But there is no crime. However, the president is supposed to judge people based on their reputation. Concerning Seselj who was so attentive to the Muslims, he had in his Main Board of the Radical Party so many Muslim members. His deputies always defended Muslims. His reputation nevertheless is that he is against Muslims and some people always exaggerate their reputation, just as they speak of Karadzic, although the higher representative recently said that the Muslims never had a better friend than Karadzic, the higher representative. Somehow this got swept under the carpet, although I was really a true friend to the Muslims, even to Mr. Izetbegovic. But my obligations toward my own people cannot be set aside for the sake of friendship. In 1995 Arkan's unit or Arkan did not commit any crimes against anyone except Serb deserters, and the very next day their powers to bring deserters into custody were revoked. I began my speech with the Drina. Until the end of March while the joint state was still in place, the Patriotic League and the Green Berets were setting municipalities along the Drina on fire, with a clear aim to bring UN forces to the Drina and cut off Bosnia from Yugoslavia. Although recognition, international recognition was already promised, it was expected on the 6th of April, it was already on the horizon, they proclaim general mobilisation. Which kind of world could recognise a country in which a general mobilisation is going on? However, the international community did this in our case. It says that Izetbegovic was against such a Bosnia-Herzegovina that was moving towards independence, and the greatest experts of this world said that recognition was a mistake, Lord Carrington, Badinter, Owen, Vance. Bosnia should not have been recognised before all the three peoples had agreed on it. So they had recognition promised to them already and they still set fire on Foca, Zvornik, Bijeljina. And of course they failed. They set fire to Bratunac only later, towards the end of April, and in early May Judge Zekic was killed, and that's when what happened happened in Podrinje. Podrinje was divided and several municipalities fall into Muslim hands as well as 80 per cent of other municipalities and large armed forces are on the attack every day. In May, after the withdrawal of the Yugoslav People's Army, municipalities were set to fire in the valley of the River Sana. And now we have to defend ourselves from accusations in terms of what we did and what it is that we wanted in the municipalities in the Bosnian Krajina, which are municipalities Kljuc, Sanski Most, Prijedor, and Bosanski Novi on the River Sana. The Prosecution does not have an explanation why the war in those municipalities started only some six to eight, or rather, seven weeks after the outbreak of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. They didn't even try to explain why did not those Serbs immediately start to implement their plan on expelling the Muslims from Republika Srpska. During that time the Serbs were offering to Muslims in Sanski Most and in Prijedor to form their own municipalities and their own police stations, whereas the Prosecution says that the Muslim police were fired. Those who refused to sign a declaration naturally opted for their own municipalities, for their own police stations, but they could have remained in the Serbian one. So until the 22nd of May, until the incident in Hambarine, in Prijedor, there was no war. On the 29th of April an order came to the police station of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina which was based on the decisions of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, saying that an attack should be mounted against the army and control of the Prijedor municipality taken. That is when the Serbs actually consolidated their own municipality and took control of that part, but they still offered to the Muslims to form their own municipality. And they tried and went to Ljubija to form their own municipality and their own police station. Then the order came that that is not to be done but that combat should be embarked on, and the combat started only on the 22nd of May because the JNA had withdrawn on the 19th of May. The Hambarine incident was caused by the Muslims, not by the Serbs. Kozarac was next. Muslim population of Kozarac passed through Serbian and Muslim lines and took shelter in the city of Prijedor, which was Serb controlled, and the Serbs actually called civilians to take shelter and to find shelter with their relatives or their friends, Serbs in Prijedor. Why did war break out in the valley of the River Sana? D3904 will explain that squarely, because it was ordered and because at the headquarters in Sarajevo they were angry. Why were negotiations being conducted there with the aggressors and the aggressors of course were hailed from Bosnia, born and bred in Bosnia, Serbs. And this is what Sefer Halilovic had to say on the 9th of December, 1992 -- sorry --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [In English] "The BH army in the Bihac region with full attention and in organising its embryo, the Patriotic League, I was in the region personally on six occasions. Therefore, the situation in the wider region from the pre-war days until today is completely familiar to me. I was even in a position to alert the government organs in that region that armed combat was being obstructed since they waited rather long and while war was raging in all the republic of BH. In this region they were still negotiating with the aggressor." [Interpretation] Of course, at the end of May this bore fruit so that after Hambarine and Kozarac on the 27th of May simultaneously in a number of places, including in Kljuc, conflicts broke out, Sanski Most as well. And on the 30th of May, they attacked Prijedor from five directions and reached the centre of the city, causing casualties and causing problems. And what happened then? Radio Prijedor announced that civilians should withdraw. And after they had lost, the army took prisoner about 2.000, as it is written. The 1st Krajina Corps took prisoner about 2.000 Green Berets and handed them over to the investigation organs. All these men had to be accommodated somewhere. Of course the government -- the authorities in Pale didn't know anything about that. They had no contacts whatsoever. This was also confirmed by Srdjo Srdjic that -- about what was done then, nobody else, Karadzic or Krajisnik. And what did they do? They requested a detention unit to be made available because the one which they had was too small so they got one in the Omarska factory, where also before that and after that other people were accommodated, on one occasion refugees and on other occasions the army, the troops of Republika Srpska. So they got what they asked for. The Prosecution says they were detained there, civilians were detained there. This investigating centre, Omarska and Keraterm, was not without investigations for a single day. Every day professional staff was conducting investigations to see who of the people there were prisoners of war and who were criminals, war criminals, and who was to be released, and 60 per cent of the people were released from Omarska. Many were arrested, many more were arrested, and many more were found there that had participated in combat. Forty per cent of those people were transferred to Manjaca. Ed Vulliamy, who was in Prijedor only once, he wrote a good report - I'll give you the reference in a minute - he says in his report: "I passed through a Muslim village outside of Prijedor. It was intact. There was just a white cloth hanging on the windows. The people were going about their daily work ... et cetera, and I also saw Kozarac which was demolished." Then there is his interview with two Muslims. One Muslim says to him: "I didn't take part in the fighting. It found me -- they found me in the street, they took me prisoner and took me to Omarska. When they found out I had not participated in the fighting, they set me free. I wanted to get to Trnopolje as soon as possible because it is safe there." That is what he said. The second Muslim said: "I fought and when I saw that we were losing, I fled home, I took off my uniform, and I saw to it that I got to Trnopolje as soon as possible because it was safe there." So two Muslims came to Trnopolje in two different ways, both of their own volition. Not gladly, of course. The OTP distorted things. Nobody says that people left -- were glad to leave their homes and their places of residence and to the reception centre, but they did leave of their own free will, in two ways, two Muslims. In the report by Ed Vulliamy, that can certainly not be said to have been inclined towards the Serbs. He describes how people reached Omarska and how people were set -- released from Omarska. And there were professionals there working every day and nobody interfered with their work. The police and the judiciary conducted the screening in terms of who was to be released and who was to be prosecuted and who would be a POW. So these are three variants. The first day here the Prosecutor said that some people were investigated -- maybe it was not the first day, but at any rate. And then it goes on to say if it was established that they were not criminals they would be released. No, they would not be released. There are two kinds of prisoners of war: Those who are captured and will be exchanged because they are not guilty of any criminal offence; and those who are taken prisoner but have committed a crime and they will be prosecuted. Why would they be released? Because they would fight again. It is legitimate to actually take the enemy prisoner until the conflict ceases and until an exchange is conducted and until the NATO bombardment ceases. I never said that it was a precondition for it to cease, but no exchanges are to be made before it ceased. So that this is also mis-characterised. Prijedor is not on the confrontation line. The fighters who attacked Prijedor are not an army. According to the law of war, they have no rights at all because they are not a unit. This is designated and marked. They are mostly in civilian clothes and they are active in the depth of our territory. Anywhere in the world that is called terrorists, but anyway they were treated as POWs. But in Prijedor in 1994, there was sufficient Muslims to massacre six Serb policemen and a sufficient number of Muslims to ask me to let 80 trucks a day leave Prijedor a day. I refused that of course and let about five trucks per day leave. That's also in the record. So until the end of the war, terrorist groups in dug-outs in the woods, in their hideouts and in deserted houses existed and were active, operated. And they killed according to this pattern, let's kill Bozo Indjic and set his house on fire. We have proof of that here. And then they would say: We have killed Bozo and we set his house on fire. We also wanted to Grozora [phoen] but she fled through the window. But we did burn her house. So what army are we talking about? These are terrorist groups deep in the depth of our territory, killing as they saw fit and whom they liked. We have proof about the dug-outs, about the combats, about the Serbian civilian victims. So in Prijedor, to which I said Penny Marshal and the other journalists, it was not the way it is portrayed by the Prosecution here. There were crimes. [In English] "There was many." [Interpretation] But in a shift, a guard who abuses his position stops to be that when his superior arrives; namely, the first -- the immediate superior is to prevent such acts and it is prevented by the state. That is my man who is preventing his subordinate from taking such action. That is my man doing the prevention. We have hundreds of examples. Here we have testimony. Say we were closed, shut off in the municipality, not in the detention centre, then the criminals came and they injected some yellow gas and the moment they turned their backs the police took us out. And you will find, Your Excellencies, examples of this kind, that the next level, the next superior level actually saw to the rights of the civilians and of the prisoners and fought against crimes and misdeeds of their subordinates, of which there was a number, unfortunately, as is the case in every civil war. Please warn me of the time. I'm not quite sure. Can I go on now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is convenient, we will take a break now and resume at 11.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In paragraph 79, the Prosecution claims that the leadership of the Bosnian Serbs and when making up these abbreviations and acronyms they were more creative than the Soviets, Soviet writers of acronyms and abbreviations. BSL or say CBS for the Serbian language. It says that they wanted to keep as many territories as possible and to ensure their borders so that they would not be permeable as far as the Muslims were concerned. Karadzic is saying something completely different: [In English] "I guarantee that everything that extends the war in an attempt by the West to enable Muslims to bring territories back in order not to be -- to beg the Serbs, but now the entire international community has to beg Serbs to give some territories back, so we have to prepare our Serbs to lose as less as possible in a firm, responsible, and statesman's manner, but that we get the main part, that is, that a state outside any federation and confederation. And what is most important, in our opinion, we must not accept at any cost any membrane not even to the weakness association that outside Bosnian borders would be preserved because it is a great danger today and tomorrow." [Interpretation] So I'm advocating peace and I'm against the splitting up of Bosnia and against the annexation of different territories and I'm advocating modesty in terms of territorial aspirations. A territory can be consolidated, ethnically consolidated, in several ways. The way that was proposed before the war and practiced before the war was what Mr. Izetbegovic proposed was the change of municipal borders in order to leave out villages that did not wish to belong to a particular unit, that preferred belonging to another unit. So that was a way that was stricter. It prevailed before the war because before every peace plan and before every peace conference that was the main issue that he would raise. The OTP say here that I did not accept the Cutileiro Plan. We did not accept the maps and I had to tell the MPs that we were not accepting the maps because otherwise we would have had a very difficult situation in parliament. And according to that setup, the Serbs had the right to their own police and later on we would agree on the rest. The Prosecutor says that even before the Cutileiro Plan the Serbs were preparing and asking for their own MUP. Well, that's why it was part of the plan because we had asked for that and the European community thought that that was justified. However, we did not establish the MUP before agreement was reached on the constitutional principles. We asked, we were setting this forth as a condition, we were threatening, we were saying things had to be done in a legal framework; however, we did that only once that had been adopted. In the same speech, I say: [In English] "If we will redefine then we have to agree to redefine, but, trust me, it can be described and calculated how much we saved with the fact that we have not fought Croats for a year and a half. We don't know. When I see young men in those areas I think: Would he be alive if we fought Croats? That is God's will, that is the truth with Croats that appeared naturally. Many people stayed alive. Huge material means have been saved. This is the best moment for us to finish the war, that a referee plays, the end on which occasion we have an excellent score and it is better that we give something back, although I know that it is hard for us and they will curse and spit on us and they will do a lot to us. It is better that we give back than to ask back." [Interpretation] So the Prosecution is completely disregarding the context in which I am saying that the territories of others should not be taken, that people should not lose their lives on account of certain territories that we would return anyway, and so on and so forth. So a false picture was created. And this paragraph 79, like the entire case against me, is false. Another way for having a pure territory is for the army of the other side to take that area, round up the population from their homes, and deport them somewhere. That did not happen in the case of the Serbs. To a large extent, that did not happen as far as others were concerned too, and this is how and why. There weren't any undefended places that had declared themselves undefended. So the army could not enter a particular town or village without fighting through defence lines. Once the defence lines would be down, the population would leave even before the army. The army would not wait for the enemy army to enter their village or town. In the areas that the Serbs took, such as Jajce, such as Odzak, such as Podrinje later, the Serbs, the Serb army, never had any contact with civilians. The civilians had left earlier on from all of these places. That's what the Serbs did. When Grahovo fell, Glamoc, Petrovac, Sanski Most, Mrkonjic Grad, Sipovo, the people fled the very instant they realised that the lines could not be held. So that was not the way in which ethnic cleansing was carried out. The third possible way was that the army that had their own government in that territory would not have to fight its way in. They would -- they could get the people rounded up and deported, but that never happened. Witness 310 spoke about seeing, I don't know, 300, 400 people at Grbavica at 6.00 in the morning as they were crossing the Vrbanja bridge. Is somebody trying to say that these people were rounded up forcibly at their homes? How many soldiers would be needed for that kind of thing? And what kind of chaos would that have meant? Obviously that had been agreed upon, there were lists, lists were made. People reported in advance and they waited for the time when they could cross over. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (redacted). That is how things could have been done. It's not that people were rounded up in their homes; that did not happen. Music talked the situation in Hadzici. Seven times his family went for this agreed exchange of civilians and every time it is the Muslim side that did not allow this to happen. They would return to the sports centre and they would wait for the next exchange, and it was only the seventh time that the exchange took place. So that's what the witnesses told us here. They said to us that we would have an hour or two to get ready, but, yes, that means two hours if they wanted to get to that bus. They had placed their names on the list a lot before that. They even paid all their dues to the state before that. They settled all their accounts. And then they would be informed as to when the bus would arrive. We saw that; however, Kotor Varos is not in the indictment -- actually, I don't know whether we accepted that. You know, at the Presidency it said -- they say: Well, the Croats from such and such a place paid money and they were not exchanged so then their money should be given back to them. So that is how they were leaving our territory without any kind of fighting before that. Please let us take a look at this, what one of the members of parliament said, the late Branko Simic in P1369 on page 33 and 34. The most liberal Banja Luka is asking for three documents to allow someone to move out. Many municipalities are asking for all of 14 documents in order to allow a person to leave. Grgo Stojic, another Prosecution witness told us here about his village, this Croat village in Sanski Most, how they surrendered their weapons and they lived a normal life. They got a lady teacher who was a Serb who came every day. The municipality paid for these classes. The Muslims went to the centre in Sanski Most on market day to buy and sell and they would return once they were done. And one day on a Monday, he says: I noticed two criminals waiting for me. And these two criminals took him to some other place where there were other Croats, they killed them, but he managed to survive. From that instant when he established contact with normal Serbs and the state organs, the police, hospital, the Red Cross, and so on, that very moment he was saved. Danilusko Kajtez is not Republika Srpska. Republika Srpska are the policemen who took him in, who took a statement from him, who put him into hospital. Republika Srpska are the doctors who treated him and informed the Catholic organisation Caritas and took care of him so that he could continue his medical treatment. And he appeared as a witness only after the war, and that is why Danilusko Kajtez could not have been tried because there weren't any witnesses. All of that is contained in our final brief. And I also sent to the Trial Chamber and the OTP everything that I have been saying. That's our response to their final trial brief. Please take a look at this, what Grgo Stojic says. He needed quite a few documents to leave. You have to pay for this and that and then you have to pay taxes. You have to pay for transportation. You have to pay for PTT, and so on and so forth. [In English] "Those who wanted to leave had to apply to leave, then were given a list of various certificates and documents that they needed to provide. After that, if there was any outstanding tax, it had to be paid. Then they would be put on the convoy list. After being put on the convoy list, they would be notified about the next convoy. The notification about the convoy came over the radio." [Interpretation] So they drove people out by radio, and that's called ethnic cleansing. There is no example of a case when official authorities rounded people up and drove them out. There were individuals, renegades, or refugees who had been driven out of their own homes that had been set on fire, committed acts of retaliation. But this is an official agency formed by ARK, that Arkan and private agencies followed. They did leave their homes with a heavy heart, but they left of their own free will. What happened with those who had not paid taxes, who did not have the money? They were not able to leave. And what about those who did not even ask to leave? They stayed in those towns until the end of the war. There was not a single place that was devoid of Muslims. The Prosecution mentions Milivoj Milincic in a negative context. Milos Milincic was the president of Srbac municipality and a member of the Main Board of the Serb Democratic Party. Bosanski Kobas is a Bosnian large place in Srbac, and before the war - we had that intercept - Mr. Milincic informs me they don't accept for an outpost of the school called Sveti Sava to bear the name Sveti Sava. In that intercept, I tell him this is their ancestor too, just like Jacob, Isak, Abraham, and Joseph. It is a Muslim ancestor, just as Serb. Still they didn't accept, and they suggested another name, the name of Mesa Selimovic, an important writer of Islamic faith. That's what I suggested. I did not impose this on Milincic. He was asking for my advice and my support. And before the war, we were trying to find a solution that the Muslims in Kobas would find satisfactory. They did not move out. They formed a unit of the Army of Republika Srpska called Mesa Selimovic. Throughout the war, they fought for Republika Srpska. They did not fight for the Serbs. They fought for the values that are common to Serbs and Muslims: Democracy and a secular state. Then the commander of that unit, later president of Bosanski Brod municipality -- those are the Muslims then who didn't have to go anywhere. They didn't have to leave. They signed up and joined the army of their own will. But Milincic made that concession before the war and met their request that the school be called not St. Sava but Mesa Selimovic, and the Prosecution portrays this lovely man, an honest man, in the way they do. We saw from the document sent by the Muslim government to the Prosecution in the beginning of July 1996 an overview of all the places with the numbers of Muslim population before the war. For every municipality, they say Serbs took over power in Laktasi municipality but not by war, by settlement. The Serbs were there in government from the beginning because the SDS had won the elections, but in all these municipalities there was a significant number of Muslims. And the table made by Ewa Tabeau shows that more Muslims left municipalities after the Dayton Accords than before. When the war was over, when the borders were clear, people started moving; until then, they stayed although they had the option to sign up for convoys and didn't use that option.
