Further, they adduce some hearsay and some allegations to the effect that Vladimir Lukic, the prime minister of Republika Srpska, had said something that is inappropriate in respect of non-Serbs, citizens of a different ethnicity. But it is a fact that Lukic never in -- had the intention of non-Serbs being killed or expelled, as confirmed by his contemporaneous documents. In this document which is D3060, it is stated: [In English] "If our enemies insist on continuing the war, we must insist on the obligations this Assembly took upon itself when it adopted a declaration on peace. Already today we must begin creating conditions so that citizens who have left their homes because of war -- because they didn't feel safe and felt their property -- save them and their property that was threatened once permanent peace has been established can return to the territory of Republika Srpska. We must guarantee to all citizens of all ethnicities all rights under the constitution and laws. We have taken these obligations upon us and we have to fulfil them." [Interpretation] Prime Minister Lukic and the government programme and the words he addressed to the Assembly two months before all this hearsay, this slander of Mr. Lukic before the Presidency of Yugoslavia, and this is what it says. It is particularly important: [In English] "And even distribution of aid to the Muslims and Croats, something the commission will pay particular attention to." [Interpretation] That is in document D3061, page 8. So the rumours that are being presented to this Trial Chamber have to do with what Brdjanin purportedly said, that only 3 per cent of Croats should stay on or something like that. That's what President Tudjman said about the Serbs, but nobody said that. We heard Sveto Selinovic, who denied that he even knew that man, this Muslim witness from Rogatica who claimed here that he had heard that from him. And we saw this witness from Prijedor who said that the programme of the Serb Democratic Party and of Serbs was that there is no co-existence between Orthodox Serbs and non-Serbs. That is one of the key points of the Islamic Declaration that is being ascribed to us, just like Tudjman's maxim is being ascribed to us; namely, that only 5 per cent of those who do not belong can stay on. None of the Serbs said anything like that. That is the situation in which it is possible to present hearsay, rumours, slander, and to promote them as evidence since there is no substantive evidence in documents or in actions. Also, jokes, allusions, irony, sarcasm, all of that is represented in its literal form and is being offered to the Trial Chamber as evidence against the Serbs. At that time, we had war declared against us and there are twice as many Muslims and Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina compared to the Serbs. And then their armies were involved and then take into account NATO, especially their intelligence services, then also take into account the reconnaissance assistance and the rapid deployment force and then the air strikes that were there by way of assistance. Excellencies, the Serbs were cornered and they behaved far better than anyone else would have behaved if cornered in that way. It was total destruction that threatened them, and the Prosecution is saying the -- some Serb blurted something out in an unofficial conversation, in a private conversation. That is how the entire Serb people have been attacked and our Western allies betrayed us yet again and they opted for non-European variance in Bosnia, although they did have Muslims of a preeminently European orientation. I see the time and I thank you for the extension. If there are three minutes left, perhaps I could present paragraph 480 as well of the Prosecution brief, where they are trying to say that the VRS -- well, actually, the Prosecution is trying to distort an authentic order, to arrest and try members of paramilitary forces for crimes that they had committed. But the Prosecution is trying to say -- trying to say that the army wanted to include the paramilitaries in their own units. These are groups of organised people, these paramilitaries. Just by being members of the paramilitary, they do not have to be people who are criminals. We disowned them and we are going to prosecute them and we did that. We arrested them, and so on. And it is the legal obligation of the army --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It has become too fast for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please slow down. You are far too fast for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could repeat from, "... it is the legal obligation of the army ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The fact that self-organised groups are being included, yes, they are paramilitary groups but that doesn't mean that they committed crimes. However, it is a legal obligation to include paramilitary groups into the army, and it is on that basis that I issued the order on the 13th of June; that is to say, to have paramilitary units become part of the VRS, otherwise they will be arrested. We disowned the paramilitaries, all of those who are not part of the VRS. Those we prosecuted, arrested, et cetera, throughout Republika Srpska. And there is documentation to that effect. 481 is the last paragraph that I'd like to deal with. The Prosecution says that Veljko Milanovic terrorised Muslims in Prnjavor before the war. However, the document states that individuals from that unit were involved in clashes with the police too and that Karadzic not only had nothing to do with such individuals but was strongly against them. There is evidence supporting this, D4077, paragraphs 31 to 32; as well as telephone conversations, D4080 and D4078, where I say to my interlocutors and they say: Not everybody is a criminal, only a few of them. And I say: All right. Have those few arrested. We want nothing to do with criminals. If the entire unit is not criminal, then those who are criminals have to be arrested. And later on, there were interventions to the effect that they should be released, and my response was - and we also have this in documents - only based on the law, only if it's based on the law. If there's reasons for detaining them, they should remain in detention. And if there are any further decisions to be made on keeping them in custody, that is for the judiciary to decide. So this was even before the war. There are no examples to the contrary. The Prosecution is saying that Karadzic promoted a policy of impunity. If that were the case, I would have to intervene with the judiciary and the police asking them not to punish anyone, and that did not happen. However, the Prosecution think that I have some kind of services for which I'm going to arrest and threaten, and so on. Presidents do not do that in any country. It is state organs that do that. And a president only harmonises and supervises what is happening. And then if somebody does something wrong, then the president can see how the different branches of government can be harmonies. Thank you for this extension, and I think that this will do for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn for today and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of October, 2014, at 9.00 a.m. 25
